alt: Reading a token list built by sys.stdin.read().split(), with a pos pointer that reads n, then moves across the n value tokens one at a time. The same numbers split across several lines produce the same token list as one line, and an N of 0 leaves no value tokens to read.

steps.caption: The whole input becomes one list of strings: ['5', '10', '20', '30', '40', '50']. pos starts at 0.
tokens[0] is '5', so n = 5. pos moves to 1.
tokens[1] is '10'. Adding it makes the running total 10. pos moves to 2.
tokens[2] is '20'. Adding it makes the running total 30. pos moves to 3.
tokens[3] is '30'. Adding it makes the running total 60. pos moves to 4.
tokens[4] is '40'. Adding it makes the running total 100. pos moves to 5.
tokens[5] is '50'. Adding it makes the running total 150. pos moves to 6.

The whole input becomes one list of strings: ['0']. pos starts at 0.
tokens[0] is '0', so n = 0. pos moves to 1.
n is 0, so the loop body never runs: there are no value tokens to read.
